OWNED FILES (new): frontend/e2e/judge-journeys.js and frontend/e2e/judge-journeys.test.js. Edit nothing else. Read, but do not change, frontend/e2e/roleplay-judge.js, frontend/e2e/blind-player.js, frontend/e2e/merge-blind-player.js and frontend/e2e/scene-runtime.spec.js (the @llm-canon test at line ~116 shows how scenes are built for the judge).

GOAL: the hosted @llm-canon test plays a stale fixed script and cannot finish. We want the same scene canon judge (judgeSceneNarration in frontend/e2e/roleplay-judge.js, 7 booleans per scene, 63 points per nine-scene run) to judge the already-recorded hosted blind-player journeys instead. Write a small ES-module CLI.

BUILD frontend/e2e/judge-journeys.js:
1. Export buildSceneJudgments(report) (pure) and judgeJourneys(report, { judge = judgeSceneNarration, scenes } = {}) (async) and a main when run as a script: `node e2e/judge-journeys.js <e2e-blind-player.json> <out.json> [replicate numbers, comma separated]`. The input is the merged blind-player report: top-level `replicates`, each `{replicate, scenes:[{scene, opening_text, turns:[...], exit_cause, transition_turn, ...}]}` where each turn has `turn`, `input`, `text`, `rejected`, `scene_id`, `grounding_ids`, `transition_cause`, `story_complete`. Read frontend/e2e/blind-player.js to learn exactly what `text` and `opening_text` contain on the turn that leaves a scene and on the last turn of the run, and follow it.
2. For every replicate and scene produce the argument object judgeSceneNarration expects: { sceneId, opening: opening_text, turns:[{ player_input: input, narration: text, left_scene: <true only for the turn on which the story left that scene>, beats_projected: [] }], revealedKnowledgeIds: <sorted union of grounding_ids of the scene's turns> }. Skip turns that were rejected or have empty text. A scene with no usable turns is reported as skipped, not judged. Call the judge one scene at a time (sequentially), pass through its verdict fields, and tag each result with replicate and scene_id.
3. Output JSON: { source, generated_at, judged_by: model name from E2E_JUDGE_MODEL or gpt-5.6-luna, replicates: [{replicate, scenes:[judgment...], score, max_score}] , totals_by_check: {protected_safe: n, ...}, score, max_score }. Score = count of true among the 7 booleans protected_safe, exit_motivated, rewards_investigation, scene_local, progressive, canon_consistent, rich, per judged scene (7 per scene). If a judge call throws, record the error on that scene and continue.
4. Print a compact table to stdout: per replicate, one line per scene with the verdict and the seven booleans as 1/0, then the totals.
5. No new dependencies. Do not call any network service in tests.

TESTS frontend/e2e/judge-journeys.test.js (node:test, hermetic, injected fake judge, no network, no OPENAI_API_KEY needed): (a) buildSceneJudgments on a small hand-made report with two scenes, one rejected turn and one empty turn: correct opening, turns, left_scene, revealedKnowledgeIds, skipped scene; (b) judgeJourneys with a fake judge returning fixed booleans: scores add up (7 per scene), a throwing judge is recorded and does not stop the run, calls are sequential; (c) the real recorded report /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/keep/canonical-x3/e2e-blind-player.json (skip the test if the file is absent) builds nine scenes for replicate 1 with non-empty openings, and scene 3C has revealedKnowledgeIds. Keep tests under 5 s.

HOW TO RUN: from frontend/: the repo's node_modules is not in your worktree; for tests run `ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/frontend/node_modules node_modules` inside frontend/ first (do not add the symlink to anything), then `node --test e2e/judge-journeys.test.js` and `npm test`. Reply with the files created.
